content: # 城市节庆带来酒店订单，先证明哪些房晚真的是活动增量

上海市政府英文信息页 2026 年 9 月 7 日发布的消息显示，2026 上海旅游节经典季自 9 月 1 日启动，全市安排 170 多项文旅活动；9 月至 10 月底还将与酒店集团合作推出"景点＋酒店""体育赛事＋酒店"等组合产品。同一条来源还提到，2025 年上海旅游节首次采用"一节两季"模式，整个节庆周期共安排了约 500 项活动，并与酒店和旅游企业联合推出促销路线。这两段公开信息只能证明城市端活动供给正在增加、酒店集团已经被邀请参与产品组合，不能证明任何一家单店将因此获得确定性的订单或利润。
在这样的公开信号面前，单店业主和总经理最先要回答的并不是"做不做"，而是"做了之后，凭什么证明哪些房晚是活动带来的"。活动订单数和房晚增长很容易拿到，活动增量却很难证明。下文给出一套先把活动增量从自然增长里拆出来的方法，再给出责任分工、最低成本测试和退出条件；所有数字仅用于演示方法，不作为任何单店的预测。
先把"活动增量"这个词定义清楚。活动增量，是指在同样长度、同一对照口径下，因为城市节庆或景点赛事介入而新增的房晚和净贡献。它至少需要回答四个问题：第一，这间夜以前会不会来；第二，它通过哪个渠道进入；第三，它给酒店带来的净房价是多少；第四，履行这一间夜消耗了多少人工、物资、客服与退改成本。

离开这四个问题，活动期间的所有房晚增长都会被默认归功于节庆。这是一种常见的归因偏差：当城市客流曝光增加，OTA 排名、自然搜索、品牌复购和价格守让也可能同时起作用，把它们全部归入"活动房晚"会让酒店在签约下一份合作协议时高估自己的谈判地位。更危险的是，活动订单和自然订单在系统里通常使用同一个渠道码、同一个价格、同一个客人类别。一旦酒店没有事先在 PMS 或 CRM 上为活动订单打上独立标识，复盘时只能看到房晚总数，无法拆分来源，也无法核算净贡献。城市活动越多，这种归因偏差越容易被默认接受。
要把活动增量逐行拆开，最实用的工具是一张活动增量桥接表，每行至少包含八列：基准房晚、活动标识房晚、自然转化房晚、净房价、佣金与折扣、兑换与人工、取消退款与净增量贡献。八列缺一不可，缺一列会让活动增量的结论无法复核。

第一列基准房晚，指同期、同渠道、同房型在没有城市活动时本应到达的房晚数。这是反事实，不能直接观察，只能通过最近两个无活动同窗的对照测算，比如去年同周、同价位带、同渠道的历史入住率或销售漏斗转化率。基准房晚决定了"零假设"，没有它就没有办法回答"这一间夜是因为活动才来的"。第二列活动标识房晚，指通过活动专属渠道码、活动专属预订页面、活动期内唯一可兑换的套餐或合作方提供的名单进入的房晚。标识方法由市场或收益部门在活动开始前确定，写入 PMS 备注、CRM 标签或独立房型代号，并在活动结束后保留至少六个月可查询的活动标识留痕。
第三列自然转化房晚，指同一窗口内、不属于活动标识但房晚数比基准更高的部分。自然转化才是活动真正产生的"溢出价值"，酒店可以为它欢呼，但不应把它和活动标识房晚混在一起计算净贡献。第四列净房价，指扣除 OTA 佣金、平台促销补贴、自营渠道分销成本之后酒店实际收到的房价。城市节庆套餐通常包含景点门票、餐券或早餐升级，这些折抵要按公允价值从房价中扣除，再算净房价。

第五列佣金与折扣，指分销成本和为接入活动而额外付出的折扣或返现。公开报道多次显示，国内主要 OTA 平台酒店预订佣金率分布在约 8% 到 15% 之间，特殊合作或独家挂牌会进一步抬高；活动期间酒店往往还要承担平台补贴或渠道返佣，这些都要进入这一列。第六列兑换与人工，指履行活动房晚所消耗的物料、票务核销、礼宾接待、客房清洁加班、前厅工时和餐饮峰值排班等成本。活动订单往往集中在少数几天，峰值消耗经常被低估，因为临时加班和客人投诉的工时很少进入部门常规预算。

第七列取消退款，指活动期内取消率、退款率、改期率和因不可抗力产生的免责补偿。城市节庆期间天气、交通、安保、票务系统故障都可能放大取消率，事先没有兜底条款的酒店最容易在这里损失净贡献。第八列净增量贡献，是活动标识房晚的净房价，减去佣金折扣、兑换人工和取消退款之后的剩余。这是判断"该不该继续"的核心数字，可以是负数；负数说明活动带来的房晚并没有真正改善经营，只是把原本可能空置的库存换成了现场忙碌和退款纠纷。

让一张桥接表真正落到经营里，必须先把每一列的责任写到具体岗位，而不是写"相关部门配合"。收益负责人定基准房晚和活动标识，决定哪些房型、哪些价位带、哪些渠道参与活动合作，并在 PMS 或收益管理系统里配置对应的渠道码、价格规则和库存上限。市场或品牌负责人提供活动标识方案，包括专属预订页面、对外文案、对外口径和合作方提供的名单管理机制，确保活动期间所有外部渠道都能留下可识别的活动标识。财务负责人核算净房价、佣金折扣、取消退款和库存减值，并按周向总经理提交活动增量专项报表，而不是把活动收入混入日常收入。值班经理和驻店经理记录兑换与人工成本，包括前台接待工时、客房加班小时、餐饮峰值补员和礼宾导览工时，必要时把这些数据按工种类别拆开记录，而不是合并成总额。总经理按周或按活动阶段主持一次不超过三十分钟的活动增量复盘，决定下一阶段扩大、试行、暂缓或退出。责任不清的桥接表，比没有桥接表更糟。它会让总经理在合作方再次约见时仍然拿不出可信的数字，又给了市场部门"声势挺大"的解释空间。

不要在签约或上线时一次性开放所有合作房型。最稳妥的做法是先选一个入住窗口、一个渠道、一个对照口径，跑 14 天的最小化测试。这里的 14 天只是一个可调整的测试窗口，不是行业通用周期，酒店可以根据自身入住节奏和活动长度调整到 7 天、21 天或覆盖完整活动周末的窗口。第一，选择一个入住窗口。这个窗口应当避开本店的传统高峰和已知大型会议，让活动标识房晚和自然房晚尽量在相近的客层结构里竞争。第二，选择一个渠道。优先使用酒店已有的直销或半直销渠道，例如官方小程序、官方旗舰店或与会员体系直连的 OTA 旗舰店，避免一次性接入多个新渠道让渠道变量失控。第三，定义一个对照口径。建议采用过去两个相同长度、相同星期组合、相同价位带、相同渠道的历史窗口作为对照基准；找不到完全相同的对照时，用最近一年里与活动窗口相关性最高的非活动周末做一个近似基准，并在备注中明确口径差异。
测试期间记录八列桥接表所有数据，加上三组补充信号：到店前取消率、到店后投诉率、复购或会员标识出现率。第一组补充信号用于衡量活动期经营是否稳定，第二组用于衡量现场交付是否合格，第三组用于衡量活动结束后酒店是否真正留下了回头客。三组信号同时改善，再讨论扩大；任一组明显恶化，先讨论退出或调整。

任何活动增量方法都需要写清边界，否则就会被误读成"任何活动都能跑出增量"。第一，高需求期的活动订单可能只是抢走高价订单。如果城市节庆与本店传统旺季重叠，活动标识房晚的净房价很可能低于原本能够卖出的高价订单，整体每间可售房收入不升反降；这时应当比较活动期间的总房费收入与无活动假设下的总房费收入，而不是只看活动标识房晚的数量。第二，淡季空房的活动订单可能被兑换和履约成本吃掉。淡季原本就有较多空房，活动标识房晚填进去的库存原本成本极低；一旦兑换了高成本礼宾、临时外包清洁或活动专属布草，这些增量成本可能反而高于增量收入；这时活动增量的结论就是负的，酒店不必为"忙"而庆幸。

第三，无可靠标识的活动不应外推结论。如果合作方不愿意提供名单、不愿意使用专属渠道码、或市场部门无法在 PMS 上为活动订单打上可识别的标签，那么桥接表的第一列和第二列都无法填实，活动增量也就无从谈起；这时应当先补齐数据基础设施，而不是急于扩大合作。第四，单店结论不应被推广为行业标准。一家酒店在某次活动里跑出正净增量，不代表同档酒店都能跑出来；客群结构、渠道结构、员工排班和履约能力都会改变结果。任意一条触发，酒店都应停下当前节奏，把活动产品转入暂缓或退出档，而不是等到下一次复盘才承认。

把场景落到一个假设性决策框架示例，而不是已发生的酒店案例。假设某城市中端酒店计划在 9 月至 10 月的旅游节期间推出"景区门票＋两晚住宿"套餐，渠道为一家本地生活平台的本地频道，套餐价位低于门店标准价 12%，单店每日预留 20 间库存，连续投放 14 天。对照窗口选择去年同周同价位带在该渠道的历史入住率。按上述桥接表记录：基准房晚 168 间夜，活动标识房晚 192 间夜，自然转化房晚 38 间夜；净房价扣除 OTA 佣金 11% 与平台补贴 3% 后约为标准价的 86%；兑换人工合计高于日常班次约 14 个工时；取消率 9.4%，高于对照窗口的 5.8%。把这些数代入公式后，活动标识房晚的净贡献约为负值，自然转化房晚贡献为正但量较小。这个假设性案例说明：活动不一定让酒店赚钱。如果不能事先跑出八列数据，很多酒店会因为活动期间房晚数增加而误以为合作成功，下一份签约会建立在错误结论之上。

把上面这套方法落到本店的最后一步，是一张可执行的管理者行动清单。第一步，把当前或拟议中的城市节庆合作写在一张表上，每个合作至少填入四项：合作方、对接渠道、产品形式、计划投放窗口。第二步，为每一个合作预先定义活动标识方案：渠道码、PMS 标签、独立房型或独立套餐 SKU。第三步，跑出基准房晚、最近两个对照窗口的入住率与渠道分布，把对照口径写进 SOP。第四步，按上文责任分工把八列桥接表落到收益、市场、财务、运营和总经理岗位。第五步，跑一次最小化测试，记录八列桥接表加三组补充信号。第六步，测试结束一周内开一次不超过三十分钟的活动增量复盘，决定扩大、试行、暂缓或退出，并把决策和依据存进项目档案。
活动很多，曝光很大，签约很快。把活动增量从房晚总数里拆出来，才能在城市节庆真正多起来的时候，让每一次合作都建立在可验证的数字上，而不是建立在"声势挺大"四个字上。

contentEn: City Festivals Can Fill Hotels. First Prove Which Room Nights Are Truly Incremental

A citywide event can stimulate demand, but it does not prove incremental room nights at a specific hotel. Before committing inventory or rate, a property should define what would have happened without the partnership, tag the demand it can observe, and measure contribution after displacement and fulfillment costs.

The Shanghai Municipal Government reported on September 7, 2026 that the classic season of the 2026 Shanghai Tourism Festival began on September 1, with more than 170 cultural and tourism activities planned across the city. The programme also included cooperation with hotel groups on products combining accommodation with attractions or sporting events. This is useful city level context. It shows that event supply and hotel linked products are expanding. It does not show that any particular hotel will receive incremental bookings, achieve a higher net room rate or earn additional profit.

That distinction should shape the first management question. Do not begin with whether the hotel should join. Begin with how the hotel will prove which room nights came from the activity, which would have arrived anyway, what they contributed after costs, and what operating capacity they consumed.
Start with the counterfactual

Incremental demand is not the same as the number of bookings carrying an event name. The practical question is how many room nights, and how much contribution, the hotel would have received if the event partnership had not existed.

That counterfactual cannot be observed directly. It must be estimated from comparable periods and documented assumptions. The comparison should be as consistent as possible on the length of the stay window, weekday and weekend mix, room type, rate band, booking channel, normal seasonality, and known conferences or other demand shocks. Two comparable non event windows are more useful than one. If no close comparison exists, management can use the most relevant available period, but it should record the differences instead of hiding them.
The baseline will never create perfect certainty. Its purpose is to prevent management from treating every room night sold during a festival as demand created by that festival.
Build an eight field event incrementality bridge

For each date, room type and channel combination, maintain eight fields. The fields are the counterfactual baseline room nights, event tagged room nights, actual untagged room nights, realized room revenue, incremental commissions and discounts, incremental redemption and labour cost, actual refunds and compensation, and displacement adjusted incremental contribution.

The test period actual room nights equal event tagged room nights plus actual untagged room nights. Observed room night uplift equals actual room nights minus the adjusted counterfactual baseline. Displacement adjusted incremental contribution equals the total contribution during the test minus the contribution expected without the activity and minus activity specific one time costs.
The field definitions matter because an event tag proves traceability, not incrementality.

First, record the counterfactual baseline room nights. This is the room night level the property would reasonably expect without the activity, based on comparable historical windows, booking pace, channel mix and conversion patterns. Keep the assumptions visible. A comparison period affected by a major conference, a closure or a materially different pricing strategy is not a clean comparison.

Second, record event tagged room nights. These are bookings traceable through a dedicated channel code, booking page, package identifier, room type code, redemption record or partner guest list. A tagged booking may still have been made without the activity. A guest who would have booked the hotel directly may simply have selected the promoted package. Do not automatically count every tagged room night as a new room night.

Third, record actual untagged room nights. These are the room nights sold during the test without the activity identifier. If they exceed the adjusted baseline, the excess is an unattributed uplift candidate, not proven event spillover. Wider destination awareness, organic search, repeat guests, competitor pricing and ordinary seasonal demand may all be involved. The property should use booking pace, channel searches, price changes, competitor supply and other city activities to interpret this movement.

Fourth, record realized room revenue. Use the room revenue actually attributable to the booking, not the headline package price. If a package includes tickets, meals, upgrades or other benefits, assign their fair value before evaluating the room contribution. Keep this field as realized revenue. Do not also describe it as revenue after commissions and then deduct the same commissions again.

Fifth, record incremental commissions and discounts. Use the contract, campaign addendum and settlement statement to identify the additional distribution charges, hotel funded promotions, cashback, exclusive discounts and other costs created by the activity. Platform terms vary by property, channel and partnership structure. A single industry percentage is not a substitute for the hotel's own settlement data.

Sixth, record incremental redemption and labour cost. Include ticket verification, concierge assistance, breakfast upgrades, additional housekeeping, front desk handling, transport coordination, temporary staff and peak period food and beverage labour. These costs are often missed because they appear as overtime or operational disruption rather than as a package expense.

Seventh, record actual refunds and compensation. Include cancellations, refunds, date changes, failed redemptions and compensation connected with the activity. Weather, traffic restrictions, security arrangements, ticketing failures and event schedule changes may affect the result. Responsibility for those disruptions should be clear before launch.

Eighth, record displacement adjusted incremental contribution. This is the decision field. It should account for the difference between test period contribution and the no activity baseline, activity specific costs, rate dilution, and the contribution from higher value demand that the activity may have displaced. The result can be negative. More room nights do not necessarily mean more economic value.
Give each field a named owner
A bridge without named accountability becomes another spreadsheet that everyone recognises and no one maintains.

The revenue leader should own the counterfactual baseline, price floor, inventory cap and test window. The marketing leader should own the activity code, dedicated page and partner guest list. The property or reservation system owner should configure the required fields and audit tagging completeness. Finance should independently calculate incremental contribution from the contract, settlement statement and operating records. Front desk, housekeeping and food and beverage leaders should record their own added labour, materials and service exceptions. The general manager should decide at the scheduled review whether to expand, continue within limits, redesign, pause or exit.

The revenue team may define the baseline and control inventory, but it should not be the only function deciding whether its own activity attribution is valid. A cross functional review is a basic control, not an administrative extra.
Run a small and reversible pilot

A 14 day pilot is a useful starting point, not a universal industry rule. The appropriate window depends on booking lead time, demand rhythm and the event structure. A shorter cycle may require seven days. Another property may need 21 days or a window covering a complete event weekend and its cancellation period.

Define three separate windows before launch. The booking observation window should cover the main booking lead time. The stay and fulfilment window should cover the actual event and service delivery. The settlement review window should cover cancellations, refunds and platform settlement. A short pilot cannot prove repeat purchase if the normal repurchase cycle is longer.
Keep the first test controlled.

1. Choose one stay window. Avoid established peak dates and known large conferences where possible. If the activity must run during a traditional peak, use a restricted inventory test and include displaced high value demand in the calculation.
2. Use one channel. An existing direct or semi direct channel usually creates a cleaner test than launching through several new channels at once.
3. Apply one comparison method. Use comparable historical windows with the same weekday mix, rate band and channel. Record unavoidable differences.
4. Set the inventory cap and price floor before bookings open. Do not release every eligible room type at launch.

5. Set decision thresholds before the first booking. The hotel should define the minimum acceptable contribution and the tolerable range for cancellations, complaints, price floor breaches, data completeness and operational disruption from its own baseline.
Watch three supplementary signals
The financial bridge should be accompanied by three operating signals.

The first is the pre arrival cancellation rate, compared with the same type of baseline. A package that books strongly but cancels unpredictably can damage forecasting and late stage inventory recovery.
The second is the post arrival complaint rate. This shows whether the hotel can deliver the package without excessive waiting, redemption disputes or service recovery.

The third is a short term retention signal, such as consented membership registration or a reliably identifiable future booking. Repeat booking is a useful lagging measure, but it should not be required to improve within a 14 day pilot.

These signals should not be applied mechanically. Expansion should depend on the combination of net contribution, cancellation and complaint movement, operational capacity and the quality of the data. A single weak signal requires investigation. A material deterioration beyond the pre agreed tolerance range requires redesign, pause or exit.
A hypothetical example

Consider a hypothetical midscale hotel testing an attraction and two night stay package through one local lifestyle platform. It reserves 20 rooms per night and runs the offer for an initial 14 day pilot.

Comparable windows suggest a counterfactual baseline of 168 room nights. During the pilot, the hotel records 192 event tagged room nights and 38 actual untagged room nights. The figures show where bookings entered the system. They do not prove that the activity created 192 new room nights, or that all 38 untagged room nights were event spillover. Total observed room nights are 230, so the observed uplift over the baseline is 62 before attribution, rate, displacement and cost are considered.

Suppose the cancellation rate is 9.4 percent during the pilot compared with 5.8 percent in the comparison window. That is a useful warning signal, but it is not enough to determine the financial result. The hotel still needs actual room revenue, additional commissions and discounts, redemption and labour cost, refunds and compensation, and the contribution expected under the no activity baseline. Without those amounts, management cannot honestly declare the net contribution positive or negative.

This is precisely why a hypothetical example should demonstrate the calculation structure rather than manufacture a profit result. The numbers above are illustrative only and are not an industry benchmark or a forecast.
Know the conditions that reverse the conclusion

A controlled offer in a low demand period can create genuine value if it fills rooms that would otherwise remain unsold, preserves rate and inventory control, limits costly inclusions and fits within existing service capacity.
The opposite can happen during a high demand period. Discounted event bookings may displace higher rated direct or corporate demand. Occupancy can remain high while total room contribution falls.

Low season inventory is not automatically safe. Expensive redemptions, outsourced cleaning, dedicated transport or intensive guest assistance can consume the value of rooms that appeared inexpensive to fill.
An outcome at one property should not be promoted as an industry rule. Guest mix, channel structure, labour model, pricing position and service capacity differ by hotel.
Set pause and exit triggers before launch

The partnership should pause or exit when the activity source cannot be reliably identified, the partner cannot provide usable guest lists or settlement details, the price floor or inventory cap is breached, or the hotel cannot reconcile the financial fields. The same applies when the settled displacement adjusted contribution does not exceed the no activity baseline, when cancellation, complaint or fulfilment exceptions exceed the property's pre set tolerance range, or when activity related workload remains above available staffing capacity.

These triggers should be based on the hotel's own historical baseline. Example percentages are not universal standards. The statement that one hotel's result cannot be generalized to the industry is a communication boundary, not by itself a project exit trigger.
The manager's checklist
Before approving or expanding an event linked product, the management team should complete the following actions.

1. Name the partner, channel, product format and proposed stay window.
2. Define the counterfactual baseline and document the comparison periods.
3. Create a dedicated channel code, property system tag, package identifier or room type code.
4. Keep event tagged room nights separate from actual untagged room nights.
5. Establish all eight fields of the event incrementality bridge before bookings open.
6. Assign revenue, marketing, systems, finance, operations and general management responsibilities by name.
7. Set the booking observation window, fulfilment window and settlement review window.
8. Set the inventory cap, price floor, minimum contribution and operational tolerance range.
9. Run one controlled pilot through one channel and record the three supplementary signals.
10. Review the result after settlement data is complete, not only when occupancy is visible.
11. Record an explicit decision to expand, continue within limits, redesign, pause or exit.
12. Preserve the assumptions and evidence so the next partnership is judged from data rather than publicity or memory.

City festivals can create demand, visibility and useful hotel partnerships. But the operating decision should rest on room nights the hotel can identify, contribution it can reconcile and delivery it can sustain. A large event calendar is a reason to test a proposition, not proof that a specific hotel has earned the right to expand it.
